## The problem

Brigade staffs sourcing billets for exercises and deployments must balance qualifications, readiness gates, unit cohesion, and travel cost across many soldiers and installations, usually by hand.

## Approach

Synthetic soldier, billet, and MTOE generators; a pairwise cost matrix combining TDY dollars (haversine distance across 56 installations with a tiered cost model), MOS/rank/skill/clearance/airborne/language/availability/dwell penalties, priority weights, and readiness, cohesion, and geographic layers; solved exactly with scipy linear_sum_assignment (Hungarian); a heuristic agent tunes penalty weights toward a target fill; a Pareto explorer maps cost-cohesion-fill trade-offs.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Supports a force-sourcing decision (who fills which billet for an exercise such as Valiant Shield) and shows how policy weights shift the trade-off between travel cost and readiness. This is a core ORSA manning and assignment problem.
:::

## Results

| Result | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Solves soldier-to-billet assignment exactly with the Hungarian algorithm (scipy linear_sum_assignment) over a multi-factor cost matrix | emd_agent.py:1193 (assign), pair_cost at emd_agent.py:366-427 |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- All data is synthetic; the cost and TDY pricing model is notional.
- Qualifications and readiness are soft penalties, not hard constraints, so the optimizer can assign unqualified soldiers: 39/75 Valiant Shield assignments violate at least one requirement (15 hard qualification violations, 29 late availability).
- 'Fill rate' counts any assigned billet as filled, so it is 100% whenever soldiers outnumber billets.
- The objective mixes dollars and penalty points; penalty weights are analyst-chosen exchange rates with no reported sensitivity analysis.
- Single-period, deterministic assignment; no baseline comparison.

## Tools

Python, SciPy (linear_sum_assignment), pandas, NumPy, Streamlit, Plotly, Folium
